title: Speed Webb's arrangers and the car that went into the canal
summary: Speed Webb and Thamon Hayes were great but unrecorded; Webb had seven arrangers, one of whom died when his car went off the road in Canada.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: It was a good band! All them bands I played with, they were very good bands. Especially Speed Webb. Speed Webb had one of the greatest bands... It's just too bad it never did get recorded. And it's too bad Thamon Hayes didn't get recorded at the time. You know? But...
Both those bands had good arrangers...
And that was very important, I guess.

Speed Webb had... Seven guys arranged in Speed Webb's band. Yeah, there's... Teddy arranged. Gus arranged. Joe arranged; you know, Joe Eldridge. Leonard Gay arranged. A boy by the name of Chuck Wallace, he arranged. He got killed in the canal up there in Canada. He went off on the ice or something one night after he finished work... They was going from Montreal back to Detroit. And they went off the road into that canal, the river... You know, there's a river...

They went off in there, and they didn't find him. Because four or five months after, the snow had thawed, and they found him. They had went off the road. As a matter of fact, that's a period when no one knew what happened to him. This happened about, well, I guess maybe ten years ago, or maybe a little more -- fifteen years probably. But that's right. And I thought that was the worst thing; I got sick just thinking about it. He and his wife and I guess somebody else were in the car, and they went off the road into that thing. Boy, that's a drag, you know?
